criteria: Complete every lab step and pass its health checks
Answer at least 70% of the check questions correctly, on the first try or in review
certificate.text: When you meet the criteria you can claim a certificate with its own credential ID and a public page anyone can open to verify it. Add it to LinkedIn in one click, share it, or save it as a PDF.
certificate.scope: Intellica certificates show that you finished this course. They are not accredited qualifications and do not lead to any outside certification.

ladder.title: Software architecture, in five levels
ladder.lead: One path from writing down how a system works to leading architecture for an organisation, built from current research and kept up to date. Start at Level 1, or join at the level that fits you.

levels.title: Architecture for Quality and Decisions
levels.lead: Turn vague goals into numbers, weigh options honestly, and record the decisions your team will have to live with.
levels.why: Most architecture problems are decisions nobody wrote down, made against goals nobody measured. At this level you learn to state quality in numbers, compare options against them, and leave a record that people and AI coding tools can both follow.
levels.needs: Level 1, arc42 in a Day, or equivalent experience writing architecture documentation.

outcomes.title: Measure quality
outcomes.text: Write quality scenarios with numbers for speed, availability, security and cost.

outcomes.title: Decide with evidence
outcomes.text: Compare options against your scenarios and choose with the trade-offs in plain sight.

outcomes.title: Record decisions
outcomes.text: Write decision records that a new team member, or an AI agent, can act on.

outcomes.title: Review a design
outcomes.text: Test a design against its own scenarios and find the weak spots before they ship.

modules.title: Quality in numbers
modules.note: Turn adjectives into scenarios you can test.
lessons: Quality models and the quality tree

modules.title: Deciding well
modules.note: Options, evidence and a record that lasts.

modules.title: Structure for change
modules.note: Boundaries that let the system change safely.
lessons: Reviewing a design against its scenarios

lab.title: Your quality and decisions record
lab.text: Take the system you documented at Level 1 and add what it was missing: measured quality goals and the decisions behind it.
steps: Build a quality tree with numbers

Write the decision records

Write the risks you found and what you will do
checks: Every quality goal has a number
Every decision lists at least two options and why one lost
Every scenario can be tested

levels.title: Architecting Agentic AI Systems
levels.lead: Design systems where AI agents do real work: tools, memory, limits, evaluation and human approval, documented so the next engineer can trust them.
levels.why: An agent is a system component that makes decisions at run time, which changes how you design, test and secure everything around it. This level treats agents as architecture, not as a feature: what they may do, what they must never do, how you know they work, and how you stop them.
levels.needs: Level 2, or equivalent experience designing systems against quality goals.

outcomes.title: Choose the right shape
outcomes.text: Decide when a fixed workflow is better than an agent, and how much autonomy to grant.

outcomes.title: Design the boundaries

outcomes.title: Prove it works

outcomes.title: Document for agents

levels.title: Governing and Evolving Architecture
levels.lead: Keep architecture healthy across many teams and many years: guardrails teams accept, migrations that finish, and dependencies you can leave.
levels.why: Architecture at scale is decided by what happens between projects: who may choose what, how old systems move, and which vendors you depend on. This level covers governance that helps teams move, and evolution that does not stall, including open-source and sovereign choices.
levels.needs: Level 3, or equivalent experience across more than one system.

levels.title: Lead Architect Practice
levels.lead: Lead architecture across an organisation: strategy, roadmap, stakeholders and teams, including the AI agents that now work beside them.
levels.why: The last step is less about diagrams than about influence: making a case a board can fund, choosing what to build, buy or partner on, and growing a team of engineers and agents. This level is practice, built around one strategy you write and defend.

series.title: Skills for the agentic era
series.lead: Seven courses for people who work with AI agents. Each is built from current research, with sources you can open, and has lessons, a lab you build step by step, check questions and a certificate.

courses.title: AI Agents and Automation for Business in the Agentic Era
courses.lead: Build AI agents that do real business work: accounting, administration, customer service, sales and marketing, connected to the tools you already use.
courses.why: Agents can now take on routine work across the back office and the front desk. The skill that matters is choosing the right process, connecting it safely to your software, keeping a person in charge of what counts, and measuring what it saves.
courses.needs: No programming needed. You should know how your own business or team runs.

outcomes.title: Run it safely
outcomes.text: Add logs, limits and handover so you can trust it and fix it.

courses.title: Cybersecurity and Information Security in the Agentic Era
courses.lead: Protect systems, people and data when attackers and defenders both use AI: fundamentals, cloud, risk and compliance, and ethical hacking in authorised environments.
courses.why: AI agents change both sides of security. They give attackers speed, and they add a new thing to defend: software that reads untrusted text and takes actions. This course covers the fundamentals first, then how to defend, test and govern in that world.
courses.needs: Comfort with a computer and a browser. Technical background helps but is not required.

courses.title: Data Analytics, Python and Business Intelligence in the Agentic Era
courses.lead: Go from a business question to a defensible answer: Python, SQL, Excel modelling and dashboards, with AI helping and you checking its work.
courses.why: AI assistants now write the code and the formulas. What they cannot do is know whether the answer is right for your business. This course builds the analyst's real skill: asking the question well, getting the data, and checking every result.
courses.needs: No programming needed. Everyday spreadsheet use is helpful.

courses.lead: Build and ship real software with an AI coding agent beside you: web, Python, e-commerce and SaaS, with specs and tests that keep the agent honest.
courses.why: Coding agents write much of the code now, so the lasting skills are specifying clearly, testing thoroughly and understanding what you ship. This course teaches full-stack development with an agent as a working partner, and no-code tools where they are enough.
courses.needs: No experience needed for the early lessons. You should be comfortable installing software.
